sources.title: OpenStreetMap waterways: the Kanhan and Wainganga beyond MRSAC's Maharashtra layer

provenance.note: MRSAC's named drainage segments for the Nag, Pili, Pora, Kanhan, Kolar and Wainganga, one MultiLineString per river. The Nag, Pili and Pora are clipped to the frame 20.9-21.75 N, 78.75-79.65 E, so their length_km is the length inside it; the Nag is first because the rivers page opens the first river, and is its main connected course only (a separate 10.9 km channel MRSAC also names Nag Nadi drains south toward Hingna and is left out). The Kolar, Kanhan and Wainganga are drawn over their whole course. MRSAC's layer stops at the Maharashtra line, so the Kanhan's and the Wainganga's reaches in Madhya Pradesh are OpenStreetMap's, taken where OSM runs more than about 0.5 km from MRSAC's line in pieces of 5 km or more (length_km_osm); the two sources meet with a gap of under a kilometre. OSM's 'Kolar' follows a different channel south-west of MRSAC's, so the Kolar is MRSAC's alone.
